page: Amazon Web Services m7gd.xlarge is a general-purpose, seventh-generation cloud instance running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by custom AWS Graviton3 processors built on ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 cores. The configuration features 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, operating at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz. Memory capacity totals 16.0 GB of RAM, sustaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware acceleration support for AES cryptography.

A key component of the m7gd.xlarge hardware profile is its bundled direct-attached storage, consisting of 237 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD. For networking, the instance delivers a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Synthetic testing reveals mid-tier computing metrics, with stress-ng recording 1531.79 on single-core and 6110.25 on multi-core runs. Geekbench scores show a 1499.0 single-core mark and a 4856.0 multi-core mark, with software compilation scoring 6363.0. In-memory performance is reinforced by Redis processing 6.53 million SET operations per second and static web throughput achieving 7.77 GB/sec.

Benchmark results highlight noticeable tradeoffs in vector-heavy and specialized instruction workloads. Extended instruction scores on PassMark and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression register in the lower performance quartiles, reflecting the absence of AVX and AMX instruction extensions found on x86 architectures. Large language model text generation metrics reflect similar constraints, managing 68.41 tokens per second on a 135M model and falling to 5.99 tokens per second on a 7B model. These results confirm the instance is unsuited for accelerated machine learning execution.

From an operational and resource-efficiency perspective, the m7gd.xlarge provides balanced compute and memory supplemented by high-throughput local scratch storage. The unified physical cores deliver predictable thread performance without hyperthreading contention. This profile fits mid-tier production workloads requiring fast temporary disk access, including relational or caching databases, web serving, build automation, continuous integration, and data transformation pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m7gd.xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the 64-bit ARM Neoverse-V1 architecture on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system provides 4 dedicated physical cores running at 2.6 GHz without multithreading, 16.0 GB of system memory, and a bundled 237 GB local NVMe SSD. Networking operates at a baseline speed of 2 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, the instance delivers steady mid-tier performance across multi-core execution, software compilation, and Redis throughput, while exhibiting lower relative output in cryptographic and machine learning inference tasks due to architectural tradeoffs. The balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio combined with high-speed local instance storage makes the m7gd.xlarge an efficient resource platform for web applications, caching tiers, continuous integration pipelines, and transactional database environments requiring fast local storage.
